verdict_reasoning: No objection survived the critic. The only one raised, maintenance-fit-1 on the linker-substituted test mock, was refuted because both failure modes are loud and the point is test-level. The fix clears a dangling pointer, frees a leaked context, and makes pg_combinebackup exit on checksum errors as basebackup and pg_verifybackup do. A committer agreed with the goal in message #2 and the brief reports v3 as mostly ready.

brief.title: Fix use-after-free after failed pg_checksum_init in pg_combinebackup
brief.problem: pg_checksum_init() frees the SHA context when pg_cryptohash_init() fails but leaves context->raw_context.c_sha2 dangling. pg_combinebackup ignores the -1 return and later calls pg_checksum_update() or pg_checksum_final() with that pointer. The bug affects frontend OpenSSL builds when EVP_DigestInit_ex() fails after a successful create, and pg_checksum_final() also leaks the SHA context when finalization fails.
brief.proposed_design: pg_checksum_init() sets the SHA pointer to NULL after freeing it. pg_checksum_final() frees and clears the SHA context after the switch, whether finalization succeeds or fails. pg_combinebackup checks every pg_checksum_init() and pg_checksum_final() result and exits with pg_fatal, as basebackup and pg_verifybackup do.
user_visible_surface: pg_combinebackup exits with an error such as "could not initialize checksum of file" instead of continuing after a checksum init or final failure.
pg_checksum_final() in src/common now always frees and clears the SHA context, which changes the cleanup contract for frontend callers.
New uninstalled test program test_checksum_helper and TAP test t/015_checksum_helper.pl in src/bin/pg_combinebackup.
author_claims: create_manifest_writer() always uses SHA256, so the bug is reachable without --manifest-checksums=sha256.
Non-OpenSSL builds do not hit the path, because the in-core cryptohash does not fail after create.
The success path has no performance or user-visible change.
The new test fails with master's checksum_helper.c and passes with the patch for all four SHA variants.
The fix should be back-patched to 17, where pg_combinebackup was added; the author later left this open.
brief.thread_state: Daniel Gustafsson calls v3 mostly ready but asks for a clearer if/else with an Assert, a Makefile rule name fix, and one helper call per test case. Raja Sai pranav tested v2 and found it correct; back-patching is still undecided.
unclear: The thread does not show a v4 that answers Daniel's comments of 2026-11-06.
Nobody has decided whether to back-patch to 17, and Daniel finds the risk/reward unfavorable for so rare an error.
The material does not say whether the linker-mock test approach works on Windows or other platforms the buildfarm covers.
The thread does not say whether out-of-tree callers of pg_checksum_final() rely on the old cleanup behaviour.

refuted.title: Linker-substituted cryptohash mock is a new, fragile test mechanism
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch makes checksum_helper.c call another cryptohash function, or moves symbols between cryptohash objects in libpgcommon. test_checksum_helper then fails to link with duplicate symbols, or links the real provider without notice. The committer finds out from buildfarm failures, perhaps only on MSVC or meson animals.
refuted.argument: The test links the real checksum_helper.c against test copies of the pg_cryptohash_* API, so the test depends on which object files the static library resolution pulls in. No existing test in the tree uses symbol substitution this way. Message #4 tested only autoconf on Linux, and message #5 added meson on Linux. Nothing in the thread covers Windows linkers, and the committer of a back-branch-candidate fix would own any breakage.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the mock link correctly on MSVC and macOS with meson, and what keeps it in step when the cryptohash API or checksum_helper.c changes?

critic.reasoning: Both outcomes in the scenario are loud: a link error or a failing test, so item 9 does not fail. Daniel Gustafsson reviewed the v3 test and asked only for small changes; untested Windows linking is a test-level question outside levels 1-2.

precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alexander Korotkov, Thomas Munro, Andres Freund
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a checksum in the last 2 bytes of every SLRU page, computed on write and verified on read when data checksums are enabled. A new GUC, ignore_slru_checksum_failure, turns verification failures into warnings, like ignore_checksum_failure does for relations.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers asked for pg_upgrade support that moves existing SLRU data to the smaller usable page size, plus tests for it. precedents_retrieved.key_quote:

last comments. As it has been Waiting on author since the last CF, I
think we should mark this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: SLRU data page checksums
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add checksums to SLRU pages (clog, multixact, commit timestamps, subtrans and similar), stored in the last two bytes of each page, computed on write and verified on read when data checksums are enabled. A new GUC, ignore_slru_checksum_failure, would turn verification failures into warnings.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The shown messages do not include a closing decision, but they record unresolved problems. Thomas Munro pointed out that SLRU pages have no full-page-write protection, so a torn page after power loss would fail checksum verification and could stop recovery, and whole-page checksums are incompatible with the incremental redo of SLRU pages. Earlier, Alexander Korotkov noted that pg_upgrade support for the changed usable page size was missing. Andres Freund backed a different approach, adding regular page headers to SLRU blocks, which Shawn Debnath said he was working on.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: With your patch, a torn SLRU page can cause recovery to fail.

precedents_retrieved.title: Refactoring of connection with password prompt loop for frontends
precedents_retrieved.summary: Consolidate the repeated frontend pattern of connecting to the backend with a password-prompt retry loop (used in several client tools) into a single shared routine in src/fe_utils. The patch unified error handling across tools but left out pg_dumpall and the code paths that prompt for a password before the first connection attempt.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author marked it returned with feedback himself. Open design questions remained: an unresolved XXX comment, and the handling of tools (vacuumlo, scripts/common.c, pg_dump) that prompt for a password before the first connection or reuse it across connections. Resolving these needed further work to avoid password exposure hazards. The patch also drew little review attention.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
For now I am switching the patch as returned with feedback as there is
much more to consider.  And it did not attract much attention either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report tranche ID and LWLock pointer in LWLock static tracepoints
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set adds the LWLock pointer and the numeric tranche ID to each LWLock static tracepoint, so traces can tell individual locks apart and compare them across processes. It also fixes misplaced tracepoints, adds a single tracepoint for all acquires and releases plus start markers for timing, and adds comments on LWLock tranches.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Two parts were committed by Peter Eisentraut: the removal of the wrong lwlock__acquire tracepoint in LWLockWaitForVar, and the move of TRACE_POSTGRESQL_LWLOCK_RELEASE. In his last review he reported that patch 0002 did not build on macOS because uint64 was used in the probe definitions, and that the probe changes had no documentation. He also asked for a different argument order and whether both tranche name and tranche ID are needed. The visible messages show no new version after that review.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
First, a problem:  0002 doesn't build on macOS, because uint64 has been
used in the probe definitions.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_checksum: add test for coverage
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds TAP tests that run pg_checksums with --progress and with --verbose to raise code coverage. The author reported line coverage going from 77.9% to 87.7%.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Daniel Gustafsson said the tests run more code but do not check that the output is correct, so they add little real coverage. The test descriptions also wrongly said --progress and --verbose enable verification, which is only the default mode. The author did not reply, and Michael Paquier returned the entry with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As written these tests aren't providing more coverage, they run more code but
they don't ensure that the produced output is correct.

precedents_retrieved.title: teach pg_combinebackup to detect deleted files where possible
precedents_retrieved.summary: pg_combinebackup would look up every file of the final input backup in its backup_manifest and warn about manifest entries that are missing on disk. This catches files deleted from the most recent backup, without reading or checksumming file contents.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas withdrew the patch because no one besides David Steele asked for it. He had mixed feelings about it: the check covers only missing files in the final backup and may give users a false sense of security, and pg_verifybackup already does full verification. Amul Sul reviewed the code but took no position on the idea.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Nobody else has responded. Hence, I'm withdrawing this patch.

precedents_retrieved.title: change SOFT_ERROR_OCCURRED to a static inline function
precedents_retrieved.summary: Change the SOFT_ERROR_OCCURRED macro to a static inline function that takes a Node *, so the compiler catches a wrong argument like the fcinfo->args bug fixed in timestamptz_date. Callers that pass an ErrorSaveContext * would get explicit casts to Node *.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut suggested changing the escontext field to Node * instead of adding casts. Nathan Bossart, who proposed the change, found that alternative too invasive for the gain: it needs more memory management and casts back to ErrorSaveContext * in many places. Typing the field as ErrorSaveContext * still needs casts to Node *, unless the function accepts void *, which defeats the type check. The thread ends there, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I started looking at this, but it seems to be a rather invasive change for
the level of gain.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit e21cbb4, as the switch to EVP routines requires a
more careful design where we would need to have at least our wrapper
routines return a status instead of issuing an error by themselves to
let the caller do the error handling.  The memory handling was also
incorrect and could cause leaks in the backend if a failure happened,
requiring most likely a callback to do the necessary cleanup as the only
clean way to be able to allocate an EVP context requires the use of an
allocation within OpenSSL.  The potential rework of the wrappers also
impacts the fallback implementation when not building with OpenSSL.

Originally, prairiedog has reported a compilation failure, but after
discussion with Tom Lane this needs a better design.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The one retrieved row, [P11], reverted a 2020 switch to OpenSSL EVP routines because the wrappers raised errors instead of returning a status. This patch adds the status checks that design asked for, so the recorded reason does not apply. Neither the thread nor the patch prose points to an earlier discussion of this fix.

From the standards and compatibility angle there is nothing to object to: the patch adds no syntax, GUC, catalog object, psql behaviour or dump format, and pg_combinebackup now stops with pg_fatal, as basebackup and pg_verifybackup already do (message #1, #2). The pg_checksum_final() change frees and clears a SHA context that callers could not free before, so an out-of-tree caller that touches the pointer afterwards sees NULL, not freed memory. [P11] is about backend EVP error handling and does not apply here.

This angle finds no objection, because the patch changes no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog, wire protocol or struct layout. pg_combinebackup's output, including backup_manifest, is unchanged on success, and on failure the program now exits with pg_fatal. The pg_checksum_final() change leaves pg_checksum_context unchanged and only frees and clears the SHA pointer on the failure path, so a later pg_cryptohash_free() on the cleared pointer should do nothing. [P11] concerns backend OpenSSL wrapper design and does not apply here.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. pg_combinebackup is a frontend tool run by the backup operator on files they already own, and the bug needs an OpenSSL init failure that an unprivileged database user cannot trigger. The fix adds error exits and pointer clearing, with no new access, data exposure or resource use. Back-patching is a stability question, which other angles cover.

The fix itself is small and matches basebackup and pg_verifybackup, and a committer (message #2, #6) is engaged. Only the test harness carries long-run cost. P11 is about EVP wrapper design and does not apply.

This is a bug fix for a dangling pointer and a leak in src/common/checksum_helper.c, plus missing return-value checks in pg_combinebackup. No existing feature, option or extension covers it. The new mock test harness is not a second injection-point mechanism, because injection points are backend-only and raise errors instead of returning -1 (message #3), and the harness follows the test_escape pattern. [P11] concerns the OpenSSL EVP wrapper design, not this fix.

This is a memory-safety fix, so it needs no user demand to justify it. A committer (message #2, #6) agreed that pg_combinebackup should fail like basebackup does, and the cost falls only on the error path. Back-patch value and the new test program's upkeep belong to other angles.
